sources.entry: Semaphore UI | Web UI for running Ansible, Terraform, OpenTofu and PowerShell

summary.one_liner: Semaphore UI is a web interface for running and scheduling Ansible playbooks, Terraform/OpenTofu code, and Bash or PowerShell scripts.
summary.what_it_does: Semaphore UI provides a browser-based front end for DevOps automation tools, so teams can run tasks without deploying from a terminal. It organizes work into Projects, Task Templates, Tasks, Schedules, Inventories, and Variable Groups. Users can run Ansible playbooks, Terraform and OpenTofu code, and Bash and PowerShell scripts from the UI. It can send notifications about failed tasks and control user access to the deployment system. The README lists Docker as the most popular install method, with a sample docker run command using SQLite and a preset admin account. Other listed options are VM marketplace images, Snap, a binary, and Debian or RPM packages.
use_cases: run Ansible playbooks from a web UI
give a team controlled access to deployment jobs
get notified when automation tasks fail
store secrets and environment variables for automation runs
run PowerShell or Bash scripts on a schedule
how_to_run: docker run -p 3000:3000 --name semaphore -e SEMAPHORE_DB_DIALECT=sqlite -e SEMAPHORE_ADMIN=admin -e SEMAPHORE_ADMIN_PASSWORD=changeme -e SEMAPHORE_ADMIN_NAME=Admin -e SEMAPHORE_ADMIN_EMAIL=admin@localhost -d semaphoreui/semaphore:latest
notable: Covers Ansible, Terraform, OpenTofu, Terragrunt, and PowerShell from one web UI
Projects, task templates, schedules, inventories, and variable groups as core concepts
Official Docker image with SQLite configured through environment variables
Ecosystem of community add-ons: Ansible collection, MCP server, Terraform provider, PowerShell module
caveats: The README's Docker example uses default admin credentials (changeme), which should be changed for real deployments
Other install methods (VM images, Snap, binary, packages) are only named, with no setup details in the README
Installation details are on a separate page not included in the README
